delta.text: Confirmed.
This is precisely the bug: at line 80, `getInteractionMode()` is invoked before `consoleProcess_` is ever assigned (that assignment now only happens inside `attachToProcess
()`, called at line ~132, near the end of the constructor). Since `getInteractionMode()` returns `INTERACTION_NEVER` when `consoleProcess_ == null`, the constructor always treats the process
as non-interactive regardless of its actual mode, breaking `ShellInteractionManager` setup for interactive/shell processes. This is exactly the bug the fix commit `4

b5d099e10` addresses by re-adding `consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;` before the interaction-mode check.

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the file history of `ConsoleProgressDialog.java` with `git log --follow -p`. The fix commit adds `consoleProcess_ = console
Process;` right before the `getInteractionMode() != ConsoleProcessInfo.INTERACTION_NEVER` check in the constructor. I inspected the constructor at the parent of the fix commit and
found the interaction-mode check occurs early in the constructor, while the actual assignment `consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;` only happens inside `attachToProcess()`, inv

oked much later (near the end of the constructor). I then searched for when this split (assignment moved out of the constructor into `attachToProcess`) was introduced.

**(2) Spec
ific change:** Commit `2b7bff8f28` ("emit 'branch' + 'push' output to single dialog") refactored the constructor: it removed the original line `consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;` that used
to sit right before the interaction-mode check, and introduced a new `attachToProcess(ConsoleProcess)` method that performs that assignment instead — called
only at the very end of the constructor. It did **not** move the `getInteractionMode()`-based check (used to decide whether to build a `ShellInteractionManager` for interactive processes) to after

this new call. As a result, `getInteractionMode()` executes while `consoleProcess_` is still `null`.
